claims.claim: Primvars can be accessed with GetAttribute("primvars:foo") like a normal attribute.

facts.fact: An appended item goes to the back of the resolved list, so an arc appended in a stronger layer is weaker than same-type arcs appended from weaker layers.
A prepended item goes to the front, so an arc prepended in a weaker layer is still stronger than same-type arcs appended from stronger layers.
The UsdReferences API creates prepended references by default so the reference contributes stronger opinions than references in weaker layers; the position parameter allows other options.

claims.claim: Prepended references are inserted before any references that might exist in weaker sublayers.
Prepended references ensure that the reference contributes stronger opinions than references in weaker layers.
Appended references would be inserted after existing references.
AddReference() produces prepended references.
The UsdReferences API creates prepended references by default.

facts.fact: Layer offsets are meant for simple retiming; value clips are the more powerful mechanism for elaborate cases.
An explicit clip set's times metadata is a list of (stageTime, clipTime) pairs that maps stage time to clip time and can scale, offset, loop or reverse clips.

claims.claim: Value Clips provide a way to retime a layer or stage with non-linear frame mapping.
Layer offsets only support simple linear remapping with constant offset and scale.
USD supports Value Clips for more elaborate animation retiming scenarios.
With explicit metadata clip sets, a mapping of stage time to clip time can be specified to retime clips.

facts.fact: Usdz files can be unpacked using any zip/unzip program.
usdzip can list the contents of a package, and the UsdzFileFormat has helper APIs for introspecting and extracting data from a package.

claims.claim: Textures embedded in a USDZ file can be extracted by unpacking the package.

facts.fact: UsdUVTexture's fallback input (float4, default (0, 0, 0, 1)) is the value used when the texture cannot be read.

claims.claim: UsdUVTexture outputs the fallback value of (0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0) when the texture file it references cannot be read.

facts.fact: Relocates can only map prims introduced via composition arcs (a root prim cannot be relocated).
Once a source path is relocated it is no longer valid in the current namespace; local opinions authored at the source path produce an error.

claims.claim: When a relocate is authored, the original source path becomes a tombstone.
A relocated source path is considered no longer valid in the current namespace.
Local opinions cannot be authored at a relocated source path anymore.
A local prim disappears upon flattening the stage because the source path is a tombstone where local opinions cannot be authored.
When a prim is relocated, no opinions can be authored at any path that has the source path prefix.

facts.fact: UsdStage::GetUsedLayers lets you count and examine the layers required to produce the current view of a stage.
usdzip --asset discovers all recursively referenced files when packaging.

facts.fact: UsdPreviewSurface models a physically-based surface.

facts.fact: timeCodesPerSecond scales TimeCode coordinates to real-time seconds.
framesPerSecond indicates the desired playback rate on playback devices and normally does not affect TimeCode scaling.
framesPerSecond is used as a fallback for timeCodesPerSecond only when timeCodesPerSecond is not set.

claims.claim: timeCodesPerSecond represents the scaling factor that maps TimeCode coordinates to real-time seconds.
framesPerSecond represents the desired playback rate when the animation is viewed in a playback device such as a DCC tool or usdview.
Camera projection attributes should not be uniform by default.

facts.fact: Valid UsdGeom scene description should always provide an authored extent on a gprim.
If the gprim's shape is animated, the authored extent should capture the changing shape.
Extents are not automatically recomputed when geometry changes.

claims.claim: Authoring extent on Gprims is required in valid UsdGeom scene description, not optional hints.

facts.fact: For a pattern-based (expression-mode) collection, explicitOnly is equivalent to expandPrims.

claims.claim: The explicitOnly expansion rule applies to expression-mode collections.

facts.fact: SubLayers is the composition arc used to construct LayerStacks.
The primary use of references is composing smaller units of scene description into larger aggregates.
References can achieve similar layering only when one knows exactly which prims need to be layered.

claims.claim: References are mainly used for bringing new elements into the scene graph with namespace remapping or renaming of prims.

facts.fact: Making a reference instanceable declares that no overrides will be expressed on prims beneath it; such overrides are ignored.
Instanceability can be overridden in a stronger layer (instanceable = false) to break the instance and get back its own children.
Collections authored outside instances can target prims inside instances (instance proxies) and be bound to materials.

claims.claim: The error 'Authoring to an instance proxy is not allowed' means you are trying to directly assign a material to prims inside an instance proxy.
An instance proxy is a referenced USD model.
USD does not allow direct bindings to prims inside aggregate instances without breaking the instances.
Collections via UsdCollectionAPI can be used to bind materials to specific prims inside referenced instances.
Using collections allows targeting prims inside instances without breaking the instances.

facts.fact: Regular attributes apply only to the prim on which they are specified.
Primvars also apply to child imageable prims unless those children have their own opinions.

claims.claim: Primvars are inherited down the scene namespace.

Non-constant interpolation modes are not inherited down the namespace.
Regular USD attributes only apply to the prim on which they are specified.
Primvars implicitly apply to all child imageable prims unless the child prims have their own opinions about those primvars.

facts.fact: Give the low-res geometry purpose proxy and the high-res geometry purpose render.
Proxy-purpose prims are meant for lightweight renders and interactive viewports; render-purpose prims for final-quality renders.

facts.fact: Downstream contexts can dynamically add new variants to an existing VariantSet.

facts.fact: Value clips can stitch per-time-step generated/simulation assets into a continuous animation without impacting the generation process.
usdstitchclips assembles a sequence of file-per-time-step layers into a Value Clips representation.

claims.claim: Value Clips are a sensible approach for caching per-frame USD files in parallel on a render farm and stitching them together.
Value Clips are specifically designed for crowd animations where you can apply the same sets of animations to multiple background characters.
In crowd animations, Value Clips allow animations to be re-sequenced and/or re-timed as necessary.
The usdstitchclips utility is explicitly designed to stitch together sequential animation files into a Value Clip representation.
Value Clips provide reduced performance impact by accessing animated data layers as-needed during value resolution, not at stage open.

facts.fact: Use an explicit clip set: its times list of (stageTime, clipTime) pairs can scale, offset and loop clips.
